title: Repeating work with for, while, and foreach loops
hook: Loops repeat a block of code. Use for when you need an index, while when you test a condition first, do-while when you need at least one run, and foreach when you want to walk every item in a sequence.

blocks.text: A **loop** runs a block of code repeatedly until a condition fails or the sequence ends. C# has four loop forms: **for** (index-based), **while** (condition-first), **do-while** (body-first, at least once), and **foreach** (sequence walk). The foreach loop is the idiomatic choice for walking arrays, lists, and any type that implements IEnumerable — the shape you want for CSV rows and message batches.

entries.plainDefinition: A loop that walks each element of a sequence by calling GetEnumerator internally.
A contract that lets a type be walked with foreach. Arrays, List<T>, and many collection types implement it.
entries.example: List<string>, string[], and HashSet<int> all work with foreach.

entries.plainDefinition: The variable declared in foreach (var item in collection). It is read-only for most collection types.
entries.example: You cannot assign to item to change the collection slot.

blocks.text: Reach for foreach when you need every item in a collection and the index does not matter. Use for only when the index is part of the business rule — skipping a CSV header row, processing a sliding window, or parallel index math. Do not foreach and Add to the same List at the same time — the enumerator throws InvalidOperationException. High-concurrency work is not solved by a tighter loop; that is threading in a later module.

blocks.title: Choosing the right loop
blocks.body: foreach for a batch of SQS messages. for when you need row numbers or index-based windowing. while for polling until a condition changes. do-while for retry-at-least-once patterns where the first attempt always runs.

items.title: MoveNext
items.body: Each iteration calls MoveNext(). When it returns false, the loop ends.

items.body: The iteration variable gets the value of Current for this step.

snippet.label: foreach CSV rows versus indexed for
snippet.explanation: foreach is the default for a sequence. Use for when the index is part of the business rule (header row, window of 199–999).

snippet.label: while and do-while
snippet.explanation: while tests the condition before the first body run. do-while always executes the body once before checking.

snippet.label: foreach mutation rules
snippet.explanation: Mutating a list during foreach throws. Build a new list, or use for backwards when deleting by index.

blocks.title: Top pitfalls
blocks.body: Using for with Count on a linked structure by habit — foreach or LINQ is clearer. Expecting foreach on IAsyncEnumerable without await foreach (covered in the async module). Off-by-one when mixing 0-based indexes with CSV line numbers. Adding items to a list inside a foreach over that same list.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: foreach over List<T> uses a struct enumerator on the stack — no allocation per iteration in modern .NET. Mutating a collection during foreach throws InvalidOperationException because the enumerator detects version changes. In an SQS batch processor, prefer foreach for message bodies but use for with an index when you need parallel array slots or to delete while iterating backwards. await foreach on IAsyncEnumerable is module 13 — do not conflate it with classic foreach.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Linked structures where index is O(n)
Condition is always true without break — infinite loop
Zero iterations should skip work entirely
Hot path without profiling — delegates allocate

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Adding to a List during foreach and not knowing why it throws. Using for (int i = 0; i < list.Count; i++) on every loop without saying when index matters. Claiming foreach is always slower than for on arrays — modern JIT often optimizes both similarly.

interviewTakeaways: foreach walks a sequence; mutating the collection during iteration throws.
do-while runs at least once; while may run zero times.
Use for when the index is part of the business rule, not by default.
60s: foreach for sequences. for for indexes. Never Add during foreach. await foreach is async module 13.
Follow-up: how do you delete items safely while iterating?
commonPitfalls: Adding to a list during foreach — InvalidOperationException.
Saying foreach is always slower without mentioning modern enumerator optimizations.
Strong answer: 'foreach for walk. for for index. Reverse for delete. IAsyncEnumerable needs await foreach.'
Using for with Count on a LinkedList-like structure by habit — foreach (or LINQ later) is clearer.
Expecting foreach on IAsyncEnumerable without await foreach (async module).
Off-by-one when mixing 0-based indexes with CSV line numbers.
Trying to assign to the foreach iteration variable to mutate a collection slot.

jsTsCorrelations.note: C# foreach is closest to for...of. for...in enumerates keys; there is no C# equivalent you should reach for on lists.
